title: In the Dark of Early Morn
description: In the Dark of Early Morn in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: In the dark of ear-ly morn, Ere the light dis-pelled the gloom, Came the hearts with sor-row torn, Weep-ing to the lone-ly tomb.

lines: In the dark of early morn,
Ere the light dispelled the gloom,
Came the hearts with sorrow torn,
Weeping to the lonely tomb.
Brought they aromatics rare
Culled from every choicest stem,
And from gardens blooming fair
Round thy slopes, Jerusalem.
Ah, the thoughts that filled the mind,
As they journeyed all alone,
For the Blessed Lord was kind,
And they loved Him as their own.
Glistening in the morning grey,
Whence those garments fairer far
Than the light that hails the day
In the glorious morning star?
List! their voices, heavenly, sweet,
As the light clad angels say,
Come, behold in reverence meet,
Where the risen Master lay.
Hail the gladness, hail the day,
Bring no spices, bring no tears;
Death has lost its power to slay,
And the grave is reft of fears.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
